# Test 20261124-161622-8cce: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10, RULES.md:5, app.py:28, app.py:60, state.json | The rule says "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." For `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}`, the tool returned `"status": "paid"` and saved refund `RF-70E0E9` without an approval entry. The code compares the euro amount directly with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so €80 skipped the approval branch. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:10, trace.jsonl:17 | The reply said "it may take a few days to appear." The tool reported `"status": "paid"` and supplied no bank or card posting estimate. The shop rules provide no estimate either. |

## Notes

The seal was intact. The audit showed no breaks across the three turns, and the automated findings list was empty. I reviewed the transcript, the egress manifest, the shop rules, the entry point, the tool implementation, and the local state file. There was no captured app-state directory.

The order lookup and delivery reply agreed with the recorded tool result. The record does not establish order ownership, delivery age, or external card settlement. The saved refund matches the amount and reference repeated in turn 3. The shop tool writes a local refund record and reports its status without a payment processor call. No application spec or performance limits were registered for this test.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.

The discovery answer listed the Anthropic and OpenAI model APIs. The in-process shop tools were recorded in the Claude Code session trace.
answer:
The [evaluation report](<project>/.nookku/tests/20261124-161622-8cce/report.md) records two issues. The app marked the €80 refund paid without manager approval because it compared euros with a threshold in cents. It also gave a card-posting estimate that the tool result and shop rules did not support.

The test seal was intact. The local refund record confirms the amount and reference. Card settlement remains unverified.
